The guard cannot fire on a partially built record by accident: System.__init__ does `for name in self.__slots__: setattr(self, name, None)`, so `warmup` is None until the warmup stage assigns it -- I read that loop and observed warmup=None in the None case. The four field names the warning interpolates all exist on sig/api.py::WarmupReport (verdict, curve, separation_peak, separation_final, steps, probes). The warmup row in ASSEMBLY_ORDER is a 4-tuple with no `produces` column, so K11 has nothing to resolve, and K10/K11/K13 stay green (K13's LIVE COUNTS still read assembly_rows=39, couplings=23, wires=19). NO POLICY WAS INVENTED, AND I CHECKED BOTH SOURCES MYSELF. sig/api.py::WarmupReport says "'collapsing' is a RUN-LEVEL FAILURE and NO signature in this tree takes it as an argument: this record is what the composition root has to act on itself", and docs/04_CONTRACT.md's only sentence on it is "**`warm_up` returns one of three verdicts, never a binary**; `collapsing` is a run-level failure." The comment's supporting assertion about reachability is also true today: sig/api.py::_stop_verdict now tests `sep < 0.7 * peak or sep < 0.15` BEFORE `if len(curve) < 2: return None`, so a one-probe curve can return 'collapsing'.

findings.detail:
THE RULING IS CARRIED OUT AND NOTHING units.py EXISTS FOR MOVED -- I re-measured every property the claim lists and two it does not.

HOLDS. `Clock.__slots__` is `("n", "gates")`; all six kinds carry `__slots__ = ()`; `Windows.__mro__[:2]` slots read `[(), ('n','gates')]`. A gated Windows has NO __dict__. `Steps(1) >= period` raises UnitError, `period == 0` raises UnitError, int/index/bool/str/repr are unchanged, and a gated Windows still hashes and compares equal to a bare one (`hash equal: True`, `eq: True`). `range(Windows(3))` and `[0,1,2,3][:Windows(2)]` still work. The documented non-fix is real: `period - Windows(1)`, `Windows(period)` and `period + Windows(0)` all come back with no gates, on the new module exactly as on HEAD's.

THE TIGHTENING IS REAL: `period.undeclared = 1` now raises "AttributeError: 'Windows' object has no attribute 'undeclared'" where HEAD accepted it silently.

THE SIZE CLAIM REPRODUCES BUT THE METHOD IS MIS-STATED, and it matters because the claim leans on it to say the cost was already being paid. sys.getsizeof alone: HEAD 64 for a BARE Windows and 64 for a GATED one -- getsizeof never counts the instance __dict__ -- against 48 and 48 on the new module. The 352 figure is object + the materialised __dict__ (64 + 288, and the dict is created by the mere act of touching `.__dict__`, so a bare instance reads 352 too once you look). So "64 -> 48" and "352 -> 48" are both real numbers and the direction is right; "sys.getsizeof, old module and new module loaded side by side" is not how you get 352.

TWO THINGS I FOUND THAT THE CLAIM DOES NOT MENTION, both filed under unfinished. (i) A Clock IS NO LONGER WEAK-REFERENCEABLE. On HEAD the six kinds inherited an implicit `__weakref__` along with the implicit `__dict__`; `__slots__ = ()` removes both, so `weakref.ref(Windows(1))` now raises "TypeError: cannot create weak reference to 'Windows' object" where it succeeded before. Nothing in the tree weak-references a Clock (the only weakref use is src/data/api.py's replay cache over Areas), so this breaks nothing today -- but the docstring's "a Clock accepts NOTHING ELSE" is written about attributes and does not tell the next reader that weak references went too, and the repair if it is ever wanted is a `__weakref__` entry in Clock.__slots__. (ii) An improvement, not a regression: pickle protocols 0 and 1 now work ("n=200 gates=('g',)") where HEAD raised "TypeError: a class that defines __slots__ without defining __getstate__ cannot be pickled"; protocols 2-5, copy and deepcopy all round-trip on both.

AND ONE PRE-EXISTING FALSE COMMENT IN THIS FILE THAT THEY DID NOT REPORT: the `__index__` line says "# so range(), slicing and % work". `%` does NOT work, in either direction, on either tree.
findings.repro: scratchpad/verify/unitsprobe.py against the live tree and against a scratch tree carrying `git show HEAD:src/spine/units.py`. LIVE: "attach ok: ('g',) | has __dict__: False"; "undeclared REFUSED: 'Windows' object has no attribute 'undeclared'"; "UnitError >=: >=: Steps against Windows"; "UnitError ==: ==: Windows against int"; "hash equal gated vs bare: True | eq: True | int: 200 | bool: True | str: 200 windows | repr: Windows(200)"; "sub drops gates: True | rewrap drops: True | add0 drops: True"; "weakref: TypeError: cannot create weak reference to 'Windows' object"; "getsizeof bare: 48 ... gated: 48". HEAD: "has __dict__: True"; "undeclared: ACCEPTED (no refusal)"; "weakref: OK"; "getsizeof bare: 64 total bare: 352 ... dict size: 288"; "pickle proto0: TypeError: a class that defines __slots__ without defining __getstate__ cannot be pickled". Both trees: "W(7) % 3 -> TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for %: 'Windows' and 'int'" and "7 % W(3) -> TypeError". Determinism unaffected: `python3 tests/test_determinism.py` -> within_process and across_process both "int 20 keys ALL EXACT / float 6 keys max_abs 0.0 max_rel 0.0".

findings.detail:
BOTH REFUSALS ARE REAL AND I TRIPPED THEM ON MY OWN SCRATCH TREES, BUT THE GUARANTEE IS NARROWER THAN THE DOCSTRING STATES IN TWO WAYS, ONE OF WHICH IS THE EXACT SCENARIO THE CHECK WAS WRITTEN FOR.

WHAT HOLDS. Trimming `Clock.__slots__` back to `('n',)` makes `import spine.units` raise at module scope: "RuntimeError: spine.units.Steps can no longer carry `.gates`. That attribute is the DID IT FIRE channel decision D14 shipped CKPT.save_period on ... Restore 'gates' to spine/units.py::Clock's __slots__". Deleting Windows' `__slots__ = ()` raises: "RuntimeError: spine.units.Windows instances carry a __dict__ again, so `.gates` is once more an ACCIDENT ... Give every kind in CLOCK_KINDS `__slots__ = ()` back". Both are import-time, both name D14 and the producer, and the real tree imports clean.

NARROWER ONE. The loop is `for kind in CLOCK_KINDS + (Clock,)`, so it only ever checks the six names hand-listed in CLOCK_KINDS. A SEVENTH Clock kind added next year without `__slots__ = ()` escapes BOTH arms -- I defined one and it accepted an arbitrary attribute with a live `__dict__` ({'anything': 1}) while `import spine.units` stayed green. That is the same undeclared affordance the check exists to refuse, arriving by the same route (someone writing a Clock kind who has never read D14), and the whole file already knows the fix: `Clock.__subclasses__()` enumerates every kind rather than the six somebody remembered to list. Low probability, but the check's own docstring says it refuses "BOTH ways the declaration can go wrong", and this is a third.

NARROWER TWO, cosmetic but it is a repair instruction a reader will follow. The first refusal ends "do not add a __slots__ of its own to a Clock kind that shadows it". Shadowing is neither detected nor harmful: `class Shadow(Clock): __slots__ = ('gates',)` accepts `.gates`, carries no __dict__, and the check passes it. The message names a failure mode that is not one.
findings.repro: Two scratch trees outside the repo, each a copy of src/ with one edit. drop_slot (Clock.__slots__ -> ('n',)): `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.../drop_slot/src');import spine.units"` -> the RuntimeError above, raised from units.py's `_verify_gate_channel()` call at module scope. restore_dict (Windows' `__slots__ = ()` line deleted; `sed -n '146,149p'` confirms Windows now has only a docstring and KIND) -> the second RuntimeError above. Coverage gap: `python3 -c "import spine.units as U; class NoSlots(U.Clock): KIND='noslots'" ...` -> "unregistered kind with no __slots__ accepts ANY attr: 1 | __dict__: {'anything': 1}" and "CLOCK_KINDS membership: NoSlots False". Shadow case -> "shadow accepts gates: ('x',) | has __dict__: False".

findings.detail:
THEIR REFUTATION IS CORRECT AND I RE-MEASURED IT FROM SCRATCH RATHER THAN RE-READING THEIRS. ckpt/api.py's cost-(2) paragraph says the tidy-up "turns this function's last-but-one statement into an AttributeError, and does the same to the four sibling producers named above". It does not.

MEASURED, LIVE, TWICE. On the shipped tree all six producers return their gates: CKPT.save_period 1 gate on a Windows, CAP.new_valve 2 on a Valve, FAB.build 2 on a Population, MEM.open_store 1 on a Store, SIG.build a 0-entry dict on a SigState, TOK.build_vocabulary 1 on a Vocabulary. On a scratch copy of src/ carrying HEAD's units.py plus `__slots__ = ()` inserted into all six kinds -- the exact tidy-up the paragraph fears -- ONLY CKPT.save_period changes: "RAISED AttributeError: 'Windows' object has no attribute 'gates'". The other five are byte-for-byte the same lines.

WHY, ESTABLISHED BY AST AND NOT BY READING THE PROSE: Population, Store and Vocabulary each name 'gates' in their OWN __slots__ tuple (I printed all three); Valve and SigState are `@dataclasses.dataclass` with no slots=True and therefore carry their own __dict__. None of the five is a Clock subclass, so nothing in spine/units.py can reach them. Exactly one producer stood on the omission.

This does not shrink the defect in kind -- one silently dropped Gate is the whole class spine/gate.py exists to refuse -- but a ruling written against "five packages break" would have been a ruling against a number nobody took. src/ckpt/api.py is another agent's file this run and the correcting edit is correctly left as residue.
